name: Aurora homepage: self-driving freight and the Aurora Driver
title: Aurora homepage: self-driving freight and the Aurora Driver
answer: This is Aurora's homepage, a marketing landing page for its self-driving freight technology, the Aurora Driver. Its most useful content is customer testimony: a Werner quote describes a pilot autonomously hauling freight between Fort Worth and El Paso, and a Volvo quote says the Aurora Driver is integrated into the Volvo VNL Autonomous. It also claims millions of autonomous miles and cites projected freight growth. It is not a detailed deployment record, and it gives no route list, safety data or dates.

sections.body: Aurora publishes this page. It is the company's homepage or landing page for self-driving freight, built around the Aurora Driver. The harvested text is dated 2026-09-27, but the page itself states no publication or update date. Its scope is promotional: it introduces the Aurora Driver, describes it as built with cutting-edge hardware and software backed by verifiable AI, and presents customer quotes from trucking and vehicle partners. It does not read as a technical report, regulatory filing or full operations log.
sections.heading: What this source is

sections.body: The page presents Aurora's self-driving freight proposition. It says the Aurora Driver integrates autonomy into a fleet, using hardware and software backed by verifiable AI. It frames the technology as delivering safety and efficiency benefits, and as handling lengthier and less desirable routes so drivers can have better lives. A quote attributed to a Werner voice says early pilot results are impressive, particularly autonomous hauling between Fort Worth and El Paso, and describes a hybrid model of Werner professional drivers and the Aurora Driver for critical and long-haul routes. A Volvo voice says freight volumes are projected to grow five fold between 2010 and 2050, making autonomous transport a necessity, and says the Aurora Driver is seamlessly integrated into the Volvo VNL Autonomous. Another quote says today's CDLs are fantastic drivers and the Aurora Driver is designed to perform like the best of them, with consistent strong performance over millions of autonomous miles giving confidence that autonomous trucks will make the supply chain safer and more efficient. The page repeats the line 'Step inside the world of self-driving freight, powered by the Aurora Driver' and says Aurora is delivering the benefits safely, quickly and broadly.
sections.heading: What it says

sections.body: The text gives these specific claims: freight volumes are projected to grow five fold between 2010 and 2050; the Aurora Driver has performed over millions of autonomous miles; a pilot autonomously hauled freight between Fort Worth and El Paso; the Aurora Driver is integrated into the Volvo VNL Autonomous; and the Aurora Driver is described as backed by verifiable AI and designed to perform like the best CDL drivers. No other figures, definitions or dated performance metrics are given.
sections.heading: Figures and claims worth noting

sections.body: A reader following AI in transportation can use this page as a primary company statement about where Aurora positions its autonomous trucking product. It shows the commercial framing: AI and self-driving hardware are presented as a way to move freight, handle lengthier and less desirable routes, and integrate with existing truck makers and fleets. The customer quotes name Werner and Volvo and point to a pilot corridor between Fort Worth and El Paso, which is useful as a signal of deployment activity. However, the page is promotional and does not provide the operational detail, safety evidence or route coverage that a deployment record would need.
sections.heading: What it means for AI in Transportation

sections.body: This is a commercial landing page, not a technical or operational document. It does not give a route map, fleet size, number of autonomous trucks, safety statistics, disengagement data, regulatory approvals, timelines or a publication date. The only route detail comes from a customer quote about Fort Worth to El Paso. It does not mention Kodiak or compare platforms, and it does not define autonomy levels. The harvested text is dated 2026-09-27, but the page content may change and no update date is stated.
